Team,

Attached is the draft customer notice for the backplane firmware sweep we talked about on Tuesday. Key points:
- Target region: us-east3 (three availability zones)
- Window: 2027-05-20 01:00–05:00 UTC (staged, AZ-by-AZ rolling restarts)
- Expected impact: brief (approx. 60–180s) node-level connectivity interruption while firmware is written and validated — requests routed away automatically by our smart routing policy.
- Dedicated/reserved customers: we will run host reassignment for Dedicated pools during the same window; any pinned single-host configurations will be contacted separately.

Notes for customers section: include guidance to pin alternative region, increase client-side retry backoff, and opt into a maintenance callback if they want a post-maintenance health check.

I've attached the us-east3 node list and the runbook excerpt that contains the rollback steps and health checks. Please review and sign off by EOD; Vivek, want to send at 09:00 PDT if this looks good.

Subject: Planned maintenance: us-east3 backplane firmware sweep — rolling node restarts

Elena / Alpha Retail Ops,

I wanted to notify you that Redwood Inference will perform a planned backplane firmware sweep in the us-east3 region on Thursday, 2027-05-20. This work is a targeted firmware update to a subset of NIC/backplane controllers that improves stability for high-concurrency workloads and resolves intermittent packet reordering seen at high load.

Planned window (UTC): 2027-05-20 01:00–05:00 UTC
What we will do: staged, AZ-by-AZ rolling restarts of control-plane hosts and attached inference nodes — nodes will be drained, firmware applied, health checks run, then reattached.
Expected customer impact: brief per-node interruption (approx. 60–180 seconds) during the node restart. Our smart-routing layer will route new requests away from impacted nodes; in typical configurations customers will see minimal effect. If you have long-lived streams or very low retry windows, please increase retry/backoff a bit for that night or pin to an alternate region.

Dedicated/Reserved capacity: we will perform host reassignment for Dedicated pools but will avoid simultaneous restarts of multiple hosts serving the same Dedicated pool. Customers with single-host pinned capacity will be contacted directly by the Customer Success team to schedule an alternative window if needed.

Mitigation and monitoring:
- Automatic request failover and per-route retries (default)
- Prefix/KV cache preserved where possible; KV cache flush only when a node is fully reattached and warm.
- Runbook and rollback steps attached; we have an on-call infra runbook and can revert firmware if we observe regressions.

If you'd like Redwood to run a post-maintenance verification against your test prompts or embeddings, reply with a time window and we will schedule it. For urgent questions during the maintenance window, reach ops@redwood.in (24/7) or reply to this thread.

Attachments: us-east3-node-list.csv, backplane-firmware-runbook-v1.3.pdf
Status link: https://status.redwood.in/US-EAST3-maintenance-2027-05-14

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Infrastructure & Reliability
Redwood Inference

Vivek,

Thanks for the heads up. A couple quick questions for our engineering and procurement teams:
1) We run a Dedicated pool for latency-sensitive checkout workloads. Can you confirm whether the host reassignment will cause any ephemeral latency spikes or brief failovers for Dedicated traffic? Will our committed throughput be impacted during the reassignment?
2) For compliance — is there a signed change record or maintainer contact we can forward to our SOC team?
3) If an issue is detected during the sweep and you start a rollback, how will we be notified and what is the expected timeframe for an observable service restoration?

We also consume some long streaming responses (server-side streaming). If those are terminated mid-response, will the client receive an explicit error, or will the connection simply drop (we need to align on client retry behavior).

Appreciate the detail,
Elena Morris
Sr. Platform Engineer, Alpha Retail

Subject: Re: Planned maintenance: us-east3 backplane firmware sweep — rolling node restarts

Elena — thanks for the quick questions. Short answers below and I can set up a 30m call if you prefer to walk through the runbook.

1) Dedicated pools: we will avoid restarting two hosts that are actively serving the same Dedicated pool at the same time. The host reassignment process may cause brief routing updates (sub-2s controller syncs) and transient increases in tail latency for a handful of requests while capacity is rebalanced, but committed throughput will be preserved for the pool as a whole — we do not plan to take your Dedicated pool offline. If you have a single-host pin, that is the riskier case; we will contact single-host customers separately to offer a migration or a custom window.

2) Change record / compliance: attached runbook excerpt includes the change record template and on-call contacts. We will also provide a signed change summary upon maintenance completion for your SOC/ procurement folder.

3) Rollback notifications: if we detect a regression during post-flash health checks, on-call infra will trigger the rollback and we will post an immediate update to the maintenance status page and send an email to this thread. Typical restoration to observable service is 10–30 minutes from rollback trigger (most rollbacks are under 15 minutes).

Streaming behavior: if a node is drained mid-stream, an open streaming connection will normally get a connection termination. Clients should see a network error/EOF — we recommend client-side reconnect with resumed cursors or retry tokens if you use them. Our SDKs include exponential backoff defaults; for your long-lived streams you can increase the retry window for the night.

If helpful, I can ask our Customer Success lead to schedule a quick verification run against your test prompts immediately after the window.

Regards,
Vivek
VP, Infrastructure & Reliability
Redwood Inference
